title: Argument Quality Assessment: New Datasets and Methods
task_or_target: argument quality ranking and pair classification
comparison_or_outcome_labels: 14k independently annotated argument pairs; higher-quality member identified; separate 6.3k pointwise arguments
domain_language: online debates and web arguments; English
limitations_or_gap: Quality/convincingness is not explicit defeat, burden, dominance, or incomparability; no structured attack graph or critical-question outcome labels
evidence_note: ACL abstract states 6.3k arguments, 14k pairs, released labeled datasets, ranking and pair-classification methods

title: Ranking Passages for Argument Convincingness
authors: Peter Potash; Adam Ferguson; Timothy J. Hazen
task_or_target: pairwise ranking of passages for opposing stances
comparison_or_outcome_labels: pairwise winner labels; transitivity filtering; win-rate and PageRank-style aggregation
argument_representation: text passages aligned to topic stance
scale_or_size: pairwise-labeled dataset; paper does not state one compact total in abstract
limitations_or_gap: Ranks persuasive passages but does not encode defeaters, proof standards, argument schemes, or explicit incomparable outcomes
evidence_note: ACL abstract reports pairwise annotation, ranking, win-rate target, and transitivity filtering

title: Are You Convinced? Choosing the More Convincing Evidence with a Siamese Network
task_or_target: pairwise evidence convincingness
comparison_or_outcome_labels: each pair labeled for which evidence is more convincing
limitations_or_gap: Evidence convincingness is a narrow preference target; no defeat relation, burden allocation, critical-question answers, or explicit tie/incomparability class
evidence_note: ACL abstract identifies IBM-EviConv as a new pairwise convincingness dataset

title: Efficient Pairwise Annotation of Argument Quality
task_or_target: argument quality scoring from sparse pairwise judgments
comparison_or_outcome_labels: 41,859 pairwise judgments aggregated into rhetorical, logical, dialectical, and overall scores; ranking accuracy evaluated
limitations_or_gap: Closest quality benchmark to multi-dimensional strength, but labels are scalar dimensions rather than explicit attack/defeat or partial-order/incomparability judgments
evidence_note: ACL abstract gives dimensions, counts, pairwise protocol, and aggregation method

title: A Large-scale Dataset for Argument Quality Ranking: Construction and Analysis
task_or_target: large-scale argument quality ranking
comparison_or_outcome_labels: quality scores and pairwise/ranking use; relevance and effectiveness-oriented quality
limitations_or_gap: Focuses on aggregate quality ranking; does not expose structured defeaters, proof obligations, dominance relation, or abstention/incomparability
evidence_note: ArXiv record identifies argument quality ranking as the central task and dataset contribution

title: ArgAnalysis35K: A large-scale dataset for Argument Quality Analysis
authors: Omkar Joshi; Priya Pitre; Yashodhara Haribhakta
task_or_target: argument quality analysis and relevance scoring
comparison_or_outcome_labels: 34,890 argument-analysis pairs; instance-level annotator reliability; relevance-to-topic scoring
limitations_or_gap: Pair labels and relevance scores do not operationalize defeat, burden of proof, critical-question success, dominance, or incomparability
evidence_note: ACL abstract states dataset size, pair structure, reliability weighting, and topic relevance model

title: Persuasiveness of Generated Free-Text Rationales in Subjective Decisions: A Case Study on Pairwise Argument Ranking
task_or_target: pairwise argument preference with rationale evaluation
comparison_or_outcome_labels: winner/preference plus generated-rationale persuasiveness judgments; subjective pairwise task
limitations_or_gap: Evaluates preference and rationale quality, not formal defeat semantics or genuine incomparable cases
evidence_note: ACL abstract frames pairwise argument ranking and rationale evaluation as the case study

title: Benchmarking Critical Questions Generation: A Challenging Reasoning Task for Large Language Models
task_or_target: generate critical questions that challenge argumentative reasoning
comparison_or_outcome_labels: approximately 5k manually annotated questions labeled useful/unhelpful/invalid; usefulness means undermining or critically assessing the argument
limitations_or_gap: Tests challenge generation, not whether a challenged argument is defeated, survives burden of proof, dominates, or is incomparable
evidence_note: ACL and official repository describe dataset, labels, code, and public leaderboard

title: ArgBench: Benchmarking LLMs on Computational Argumentation Tasks
task_or_target: multi-task computational argumentation including quality assessment and reasoning
comparison_or_outcome_labels: 46 tasks across argument mining, perspective assessment, quality assessment, reasoning, and generation; task-specific labels
argument_representation: mixed datasets: argumentative text, relations, reasoning items
domain_language: multiple domains and datasets; primarily English
limitations_or_gap: Broad suite includes quality and reasoning but is not a dedicated benchmark for pairwise strength plus defeat/dominance/incomparability; heterogeneous task metrics complicate construct validity
evidence_note: ACL abstract and official data repository state 46 tasks, 33 datasets, five skill groups, and splits

title: CEDAR: A Chinese Evaluation Dataset for Computational Argumentation
task_or_target: argument mining, quality evaluation, and debate-result prediction
comparison_or_outcome_labels: claim/stance/evidence plus rhetorical figures, roles, modality, time, and debate results; result label is an outcome proxy
argument_representation: complete debate transcripts and structured labels
limitations_or_gap: Debate-result prediction is not argument-level defeat or dominance; no explicit incomparability/underdetermination label and no proof-burden semantics
evidence_note: ACL search record and official repository describe 600 debates, 318 topics, labels, and artifact

title: The Fourth International Competition on Computational Models of Argumentation (ICCMA'21): Call for Benchmarks
task_or_target: formal abstract/structured argumentation solver evaluation
comparison_or_outcome_labels: acceptance and reasoning tasks under multiple semantics; credulous/sceptical acceptance, extension and enumeration tasks; solver correctness is ground truth
argument_representation: abstract argumentation frameworks and structured instances
limitations_or_gap: Excellent for defeat/acceptance semantics but not natural-language expert judgments of strength; standard tasks generally force acceptance decisions rather than graded strength or incomparability
evidence_note: Official ICCMA benchmark/solver documents define benchmark selection and DC/DN acceptance tasks

title: Audiences and Argument Strength
task_or_target: argument ranking under audiences and values
comparison_or_outcome_labels: ranking-based semantics compare individual arguments; audience/value settings can alter relative strength
domain_language: formal; benchmark instances for solver comparison
limitations_or_gap: Directly targets argument strength/ranking, but formal instances lack natural-language arguments, human/expert pairwise judgments, and an explicit incomparable label in the benchmark task
evidence_note: Official competition paper describes comparison of individual arguments and ranking-based semantics with audiences/values

title: Towards Ranking Arguments in Incomplete Argumentation Frameworks
task_or_target: ranking arguments when attacks are incomplete or uncertain
comparison_or_outcome_labels: ranking semantics over incomplete frameworks; incompleteness is structural uncertainty rather than human preference
scale_or_size: benchmark paper/instances not fully enumerated in search record
limitations_or_gap: Useful for uncertainty and possible incomparability, but not a corpus of textual arguments and not an expert-judgment benchmark of argument quality
evidence_note: Official paper explicitly frames ranking semantics for incomplete argumentation frameworks

title: A Comparative Study of Ranking-based Semantics for Abstract Argumentation
task_or_target: compare rank-orderings of arguments under competing ranking semantics
comparison_or_outcome_labels: rank order, ties or equivalence may emerge from semantics; formal acceptability only
domain_language: formal; synthetic/benchmark AFs described by study
limitations_or_gap: Methodological comparison rather than a maintained natural-language benchmark; no burden-of-proof or expert support labels
evidence_note: ArXiv record states ranking-based semantics rank-order arguments from most to least acceptable

title: Argument Reasoning Tasks (ART)
task_or_target: missing-premise, warrant, and argument-reasoning tasks
comparison_or_outcome_labels: multiple-choice labels for missing components and reasoning structures; performance indicates reasoning competence
argument_representation: argument contexts and structured argument components
scale_or_size: 16 task types from four argumentation structures
limitations_or_gap: Tests reconstruction of warrants and argument components, not pairwise strength, defeat outcome, dominance, or incomparability
evidence_note: Official repository describes ART as a large-scale benchmark with 16 task types and multiple-choice reasoning questions

title: ConQRet: Controversial Questions for Argumentation and Retrieval
task_or_target: controversial-query evidence retrieval and argument generation
comparison_or_outcome_labels: stance-separated relevant documents and generated arguments; relevance/stance are proxies for support
argument_representation: controversial queries, evidence documents, and generated arguments
limitations_or_gap: Supports evidence retrieval and stance-aware argument generation, but does not provide expert pairwise argument strength, defeat, burden, or incomparability labels
evidence_note: Official repository states 98 topics, 6,500 documents, stance-separated evidence, and released benchmark

title: Detecting Winning Arguments with Large Language Models and Persuasion Strategies
task_or_target: detect winning/persuasive arguments with strategy-aware analysis
comparison_or_outcome_labels: winner or winning-argument labels plus persuasion-strategy annotations
limitations_or_gap: Winningness is an outcome proxy and may conflate audience persuasion with logical support; no formal attack graph, proof burden, or explicit incomparability
evidence_note: ACL search record says topic-annotated version is publicly released for argument quality assessment

title: UKPConvArg1 / UKPConvArg2 convincingness corpora
task_or_target: pairwise convincingness and argument quality prediction
comparison_or_outcome_labels: pairwise convincingness comparisons and scalar/rank-derived labels across debate arguments
scale_or_size: corpus family used as baseline and source in later pairwise work
limitations_or_gap: Foundational convincingness benchmark but still lacks explicit defeat/critical-question state transitions, burden-of-proof labels, and incomparability
evidence_note: Later ACL work explicitly identifies UKPConvArg1 as an exhaustive pairwise comparison corpus

title: Learning From Revisions: Quality Assessment of Claims in Argumentation at Scale
authors: Gabriella Skitalinskaya; Jonas Klaff; Henning Wachsmuth
task_or_target: better-claim pair classification and ranking all revisions of a claim
comparison_or_outcome_labels: over 377k claim revision pairs; pairwise better-claim labels and version rankings
argument_representation: claims and revisions in structured online argumentation
domain_language: politics, ethics, entertainment, and other Kialo topics; English
limitations_or_gap: Very strong pairwise/ranking scale, but revision quality is not defeat or support strength; no explicit attacks, burdens, critical-question outcomes, or incomparable/abstain class
evidence_note: ACL abstract states both ranking tasks, corpus scale, Kialo source, and released data/scripts

title: Which Side Are You On? A Multi-task Dataset for End-to-End Argument Summarisation and Evaluation
resource_or_benchmark: argument mining and evaluation multi-task dataset
task_or_target: evidence convincingness ranking and human preference ranking for debate essays
comparison_or_outcome_labels: evidence convincingness ranking; human preference ranking; quality dimensions used for essay evaluation
scale_or_size: multi-task dataset; exact total varies by task
limitations_or_gap: Includes preference and convincingness signals but does not make defeat relation, burden of proof, dominance, or incomparability first-class labels
evidence_note: ACL abstract enumerates evidence detection, evidence convincingness ranking, human preference ranking, and quality evaluation tasks
